description:
Around the year 1000, the astronomer Ibn Yunus worked in Cairo on a zij: a book of tables that told you where the Sun, Moon and planets would be on any given day. It turned years of watching the sky into something people could actually use.

We're doing the same thing in 48 hours, with satellites doing the watching.

We're students from Alexandria STEM School, one of Egypt's selective science and engineering high schools. We build real, working tools on NASA data, not slide decks.
